sentences.en: Take it away, Patrick.

sentences.en: So I'll start off with a little bit of a rant.
sentences.zh: 那我就先发泄一点小情绪吧。

sentences.en: Pre versus post increment.
sentences.zh: 前置自增与后置自增。

sentences.en: So I got into a discussion with people at work.
sentences.zh: 我和公司的同事们讨论了这个话题。

sentences.en: And for a long time, I have always just done.
sentences.zh: 而且很长一段时间以来，我一直都是这么做的。

sentences.en: So the biggest example is in a for loop, in the final variable change parameter, the normal one you do is an increment, a plus plus.
sentences.zh: 最典型的例子就是在 for 循环中，在最后的变量改变参数里，通常大家都会用自增，也就是加加。

sentences.en: And so I do I plus plus or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以我就会写 i 加加之类的。

sentences.en: So for I equals zero, I is less than 10, I plus plus.
sentences.zh: 所以，for (i 等于 0，i 小于 10，i 加加)。

sentences.en: I've just always done it this way.
sentences.zh: 我一直都是这么写的。

sentences.en: And if I put an increment on a line by itself, I do the plus plus.
sentences.zh: 而且如果我把自增单独放在一行，我就会用加加。

sentences.en: It just reads more naturally to me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说读起来更自然。

sentences.en: Like this variable, you're taking the variable and you're incrementing it.
sentences.zh: 就像这个变量，你获取这个变量然后对其进行自增。

sentences.en: You're not incrementing something that you're going to read later.
sentences.zh: 你不是在自增一个稍后要读取的东西。

sentences.en: So and then, of course, if you put it in line with other stuff, I actually tend to try to
sentences.zh: 所以，当然了，如果你把它和其他东西写在同一行，我其实往往会尽量

sentences.en: avoid that like in a statement because I actually find like I will do it occasionally, but I find it to be a more cognitive load.
sentences.zh: 避免这种情况，比如在一条语句中，因为我发现——虽然我偶尔也会这么做——但我发现这会增加认知负荷。

sentences.en: So I'd rather either have it be a post increment so that it just happens at the end and it's like I put it on another line or do it on a separate line all by itself.
sentences.zh: 所以我宁愿把它改成后置自增，这样它就在最后发生，就好像我把它放到了另一行，或者干脆把它单独放在一行。

sentences.en: And so someone pointed out to me one of my code reviews that I was doing post increment and that the quote unquote standard we were using was pre-increment.
sentences.zh: 所以在一次代码审查中，有人指出我一直在用后置自增，并且我们所谓的“标准”其实是前置自增。

sentences.en: And I said, no, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 我说，不对，这不是真的。

sentences.en: And so then I went through all of like I wrote a grep command to grep through all of our code.
sentences.zh: 于是我检查了所有代码——我写了一个 grep 命令来搜索我们所有的代码。

sentences.en: And sure enough, except for just a couple of small other cases from other people, every one of the team had been doing pre-increment except me.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，除了其他人偶尔写的一些小地方之外，团队里的每个人用的都是前置自增，只有我不是。

sentences.en: And all the code checked in that was post increment, every single one of them except those like two other cases was me.
sentences.zh: 所有提交的代码里，凡是后置自增的，除了那另外两处之外，百分之百全都是我写的。

sentences.en: And it was like, oh, it was like one of those sinking moments where like I was hoping to be triumphant because like, oh, I see everyone's using post increment.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，哦，那真是一个让人心碎的时刻，本来我还指望能扬眉吐气呢，心想“哈哈，你看大家都在用后置自增”。

sentences.en: Sometimes there's no standard.
sentences.zh: 有时根本没有什么标准。

sentences.en: And then it was like, yeah, I'm wrong.
sentences.zh: 然后结果就是，好吧，我错了。

sentences.en: That's the worst is when the worst is when like.
sentences.zh: 最糟糕的是当……最糟糕的是当这种时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, like it's too late at that point.
sentences.zh: 对啊，就好像到那个时候已经太晚了。

sentences.en: You know, like when the project starts, you can try to fight for what you believe in.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，项目刚开始的时候，你可以为你信仰的东西去争取。

sentences.en: But if it's been going on for six months and you've been doing it one way and everyone in the team has been doing it another way, then you just have to bite the bullet, man.
sentences.zh: 但如果项目已经进行了六个月，你一直用一种方式，而团队里的所有人都用另一种方式，那你只能硬着头皮接受了，老兄。

sentences.en: So I did.
sentences.zh: 所以我接受了。

sentences.en: So I swallowed my pride and submitted a change to convert all of my post increments to pre-increments.
sentences.zh: 于是我咽下自尊，提交了一个修改，把我所有的后置自增全都改成了前置自增。

sentences.en: But I still catch myself writing the post increments and then having to fix it later.
sentences.zh: 但我发现自己还是经常忍不住写后置自增，然后再回过头去修改。

sentences.en: Yeah, I feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我也有同感。

sentences.en: I mean, like compilers now are so smart that the difference is kind of negligible, if anything.
sentences.zh: 我是说，现在的编译器太聪明了，它们的区别基本上可以忽略不计，甚至根本没有区别。

sentences.en: Like, I don't even know if the instructions end up different at the end, you know, because like if one really was better than the other, the compiler, I mean, you know, there's no
sentences.zh: 比如，我甚至不知道最后生成的指令到底有没有不同，你知道的，因为如果某种方式真的比另一种好，编译器——我是说，你知道的，根本没

sentences.en: way to, there's no way that I know of, actually, I guess maybe if you used a comma, right?
sentences.zh: 办法……据我所知，其实没有办法，哦，我想也许如果你用了逗号运算符，对吧？

sentences.en: Like if you had I++ comma and then like some more logic here versus the, like that's the only way where putting the prefix versus post fix, you know, and this other logic also had
sentences.zh: 比如如果你写了 `i++` 逗号，然后在这里加上更多逻辑，相比之下——这才是唯一能让前置和后置产生区别的方法，你知道的，如果这另一段逻辑里也

sentences.en: an I, like print I, that's the only way where you could end up with different behavior by swapping them.
sentences.zh: 包含一个 `i`，比如打印 `i`，那才是唯一可能因为交换它们而导致行为不同的情况。

sentences.en: And nobody does that, right?
sentences.zh: 而且根本没人会那么写，对吧？

sentences.en: No, I would not allow that in a code review.
sentences.zh: 对，代码审查时我是绝对不会允许这种代码通过的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's terrible.
sentences.zh: 对，那太糟糕了。

sentences.en: So anyways, I just have this bad, like, I guess I looked it up at one point.
sentences.zh: 所以不管怎样，我就是有这个坏习惯——我记得我曾经查过一次。

sentences.en: I think they said it was like the original, the C book or whatever, Carnegie, Richard, Richard
sentences.zh: 我想他们说的是原版的 C 语言那本书什么的，卡耐基、理查德、理查德

sentences.en: Cunningham, something, anyways, Cunningham.
sentences.zh: 坎宁安，不管怎样，是坎宁安。

sentences.en: Oh, why do I always forget the name?
sentences.zh: 噢，为什么我总是记不住名字？

sentences.en: Wait, so someone in your code review quoted a C book?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以你们在做代码审查时有人引用了一本 C 语言的书？

sentences.en: No, the C programming book by Cunningham.
sentences.zh: 不，是坎宁安写的《C 程序设计语言》。

sentences.en: Oh man, I always, always mess up the name.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我总是把名字记错。

sentences.en: Anyways, and in that one, I think is where Brian Cunningham and Dennis Ritchie, I was combining the two.
sentences.zh: 总之，在那本书里，我想布莱恩·坎宁安和丹尼斯·里奇——我刚才把这两个人搞混了。

sentences.en: Okay, brain fart.
sentences.zh: 好吧，脑子短路了。

sentences.en: In this book, they do the post-increment like I did, and so like, I guess maybe it's being from the States and going to college here in the United States, like the de facto way
sentences.zh: 在这本书里，他们写后置自增的方式就跟我一样，所以我想，也许是因为我来自美国，而且是在美国的大学上学，所以这种写法就成了

sentences.en: is writing it this way.
sentences.zh: 事实上的标准写法。

sentences.en: But I guess people from other places don't, they use the pre-increment, and so that's just what they're used to.
sentences.zh: 但我想其他地方的人不这么写，他们用前置自增，所以他们就习惯了那种写法。

sentences.en: And then it's defensible to them, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想对他们来说这自然是站得住脚的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: But everyone I've ever seen until that day had always done, like, and then it's like, like, everyone on the team was doing pre-increment.
sentences.zh: 但在那天之前我见过的所有人，一直以来都……然后就变成，团队里的每个人都在用前置自增。

sentences.en: I'm just like, what?
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，什么鬼？

sentences.en: How am I the only one out here?
sentences.zh: 为什么这里只有我一个人是个异类？

sentences.en: I've never, like, been fussed at for this before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从来没有因为这个被责备过。

sentences.en: You should, you should, you should just have a comment.
sentences.zh: 你应该——你应该加一条注释。

sentences.en: You should write a regex that puts a comment in sort of every for loop, and it just says like this, the only pre-increment symbol should be Merica.
sentences.zh: 你应该写一个正则表达式，在每个 for 循环里自动插入一条注释，上面写着：唯一的前置自增符号应该属于美利坚。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我瞎说的。

sentences.en: So I'm just curious.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是有点好奇。

sentences.en: Okay, but you're also post-increment.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但你也是个后置自增党。

sentences.en: So I'm trying to figure out where the pre-verse post came from.
sentences.zh: 所以我正在试图弄清楚前置和后置之争到底是从哪来的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there was somebody on my team.
sentences.zh: 我以前的团队里确实有这么一个人。

sentences.en: Like, so in a for loop, it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 你看，在 for 循环里，这其实无所谓。

sentences.en: Like, I don't think there's, anyone can really make an argue that it matters from a compiler perspective.
sentences.zh: 我觉得不会有人能从编译器的角度证明这有什么实质区别。

sentences.en: So there has to be just, like, a legacy or, like, a, you know, guideline.
sentences.zh: 所以这肯定只是某种历史遗留问题，或者说是一种编码规范。

sentences.en: There was someone on my last team who was really into the pre-increment, and that person was from, like, Suriname, like, former or post-British Guyana, like, South America.
sentences.zh: 我上一团队里有个人非常推崇前置自增，那个人来自苏里南，也就是以前的英属圭亚那，在南美洲。

sentences.en: And so maybe it is, like, an American verse.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这真的跟地域有关。

sentences.en: Like, maybe people, like, Europeans and South Americans learned pre-increment, and we learned post-increment somehow.
sentences.zh: 也许欧洲人和南美洲人学的是前置自增，而我们不知怎么的就学了后置自增。

sentences.en: I don't really know how that happened.
sentences.zh: 我真不知道这是怎么发生的。

sentences.en: I have, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我确实……

sentences.en: I have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我毫无头绪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Anyways, that's my rant.
sentences.zh: 总之，这就是我的满腹牢骚。

sentences.en: So on to an interesting topic.
sentences.zh: 那么接下来聊个有趣的话题。

sentences.en: I was talking to someone about cooking.
sentences.zh: 我之前和别人聊起了烹饪。

sentences.en: And so I actually enjoy cooking, and I don't do it as much as I should.
sentences.zh: 其实我挺喜欢做饭的，虽然没有想象中做得那么多。

sentences.en: I'm pretty busy at work, but I do enjoy when I do it and baking.
sentences.zh: 我在工作上挺忙的，但我很享受做饭和烘焙的过程。

sentences.en: I've been baking bread recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近一直在烤面包。

sentences.en: I have, like, a, not a New Year's resolution, but, like, kind of a goal this year to...
sentences.zh: 我给自己定了个类似的目标——虽说不是新年决心，但有点像今年的一个计划……

sentences.en: It doesn't last long, right?
sentences.zh: 不过这计划持续不了多久吧？

sentences.en: My parents used to bake bread, and it was, like, a brick two days later.
sentences.zh: 我父母以前也烤面包，但两天后它硬得跟砖头一样。

sentences.en: You pretty much have to eat it that day.
sentences.zh: 你基本上得在当天把它吃完。

sentences.en: No, well, I don't end up having that much leftover after the first day, but I don't make a lot of it, and it does tend to last two or three days at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 不，其实第一天之后我不会剩下太多，因为我做得不多，而且它通常至少能放两到三天。

sentences.en: And then I typically either am tired of it or get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 然后我通常要么是吃腻了，要么就把它处理掉了。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: You must be doing a better job.
sentences.zh: 那你一定做得更好。

sentences.en: I don't know that.
sentences.zh: 这点我可说不准。

sentences.en: Maybe I...
sentences.zh: 也许我……

sentences.en: No, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 不，我不知道。

sentences.en: But then I was, like, talking to people, like, oh, no, I can't cook, whatever.
sentences.zh: 但当时我和别人聊天，有人说“哦，不行，我不会做饭”之类的。

sentences.en: And I'm, like, well, you get instructions.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，得了吧，这上面有说明书的。

sentences.en: It's, like, reading a program, and you just, like, follow the thing that recipe has.
sentences.zh: 这就跟看程序一样，你只要照着食谱上的步骤做就行了。

sentences.en: Yeah, you really can't go wrong.
sentences.zh: 对啊，按这个做绝对不会出错。

sentences.en: Well, but I find out, like, it's actually very rare for people to follow recipes.
sentences.zh: 不过我发现，其实很少有人会真的照着食谱做。

sentences.en: I think part of it is you have to fail.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因在于你必须经历失败。

sentences.en: Like, for example, the first time I learned how to cook, I was just completely on my own.
sentences.zh: 比如，我第一次学做饭的时候，完全是靠自己摸索。

sentences.en: And, you know, they told me to, like, put the rice in.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们告诉我要把米放进去。

sentences.en: I just was making rice, like, the simplest thing.
sentences.zh: 我只是在煮饭，最简单的事情。

sentences.en: They told me to put the rice in, put the water in, and then boil it or, like, simmer it for,
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我把米放进去，加水，然后煮沸或者说文火慢炖

sentences.en: I don't remember how many minutes, right?
sentences.zh: 我不记得要煮多少分钟了，对吧？

sentences.en: But I left it on hot.
sentences.zh: 但我一直开着大火。

sentences.en: And I guess, you know, when you're supposed to simmer, you're supposed to put it on low.
sentences.zh: 我想，当你需要文火慢炖的时候，其实应该开小火。

sentences.en: And it didn't say simmer on low.
sentences.zh: 但食谱上没说“用小火慢炖”。

sentences.en: It just said simmer, so I don't know what that meant.
sentences.zh: 它只说了“慢炖”，所以我根本不知道那是什么意思。

sentences.en: And I left, I came back, and, like, even, like, the pan itself was ruined.
sentences.zh: 等我离开一会儿回来后，发现连平底锅本身都毁了。

sentences.en: Like, the rice had just kind of, like, destroyed the enamel, like the Teflon on the pan.
sentences.zh: 米饭直接把锅里的涂层，也就是锅里的特氟龙给烧坏了。

sentences.en: But the point is, like, you know, either you get formal training, or you just, like, make mistakes like that and destroy things.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，要么你接受过专业培训，要么你就会像这样犯错并把东西搞砸。

sentences.en: And I think, like, what you're talking about is actually a metaphor for a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们刚才聊的这个其实可以作为很多事情的隐喻。

sentences.en: Like, there are people who are just afraid to, like, take kind of chances and, like, the ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 比如有些人就是害怕去冒险，害怕面对这种不确定性。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's, like, afraid probably is, like, very, is too strong language.
sentences.zh: 我不知道“害怕”这个词是不是用得有点太重了。

sentences.en: But it's more just, like, oh, this is really ambiguous.
sentences.zh: 但这更像是一种“哦，这太含糊不清了”。

sentences.en: This is really hard.
sentences.zh: “这太难了。”

sentences.en: I'm not going to try this.
sentences.zh: “我才不要尝试呢。”

sentences.en: Versus I'm going to, like, fill in all the ambiguity, you know, by chance, and then see what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则会通过碰运气来填补所有的不确定性，然后看会发生什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I guess it's somewhat, like, people who, so you can make mistakes, like what you're saying, or, like, where there's ambiguity in the instructions.
sentences.zh: 我想这有点像——就像你说的，你可能会犯错，或者说明书里有含糊不清的地方。

sentences.en: But let me, all sorts of people who it's, like, well, I've never made this dish before.

sentences.en: But, you know, I feel like I can do better than what this person's saying.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得我能比这上面说的做得更好。

sentences.en: Okay, that's kind of egregious.

sentences.en: But, like, people I talk to do this kind of stuff.

sentences.en: Like, oh, I'll substitute, you know, it says, like, you know, X amount of flour.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我要替换掉它，上面写着需要多少多少量的面粉。

sentences.en: Well, the only flour I have is, like, almond flour.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我家里唯一的面粉是杏仁粉。

sentences.en: So, like, it'll be okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，应该也没问题吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And some of it's, like, not knowing, but it's just people don't, like, the more I don't know,
sentences.zh: 有时候这倒不是因为不懂，而是人们就是不喜欢——我越是不懂，

sentences.en: the more I try to, like, follow some guideposts, like the instructions or a YouTube video or, like, something.
sentences.zh: 我就越会试图去遵循一些指导原则，比如说明书、YouTube 视频或者之类的内容。

sentences.en: I don't pretend like I know better.
sentences.zh: 我可不会假装自己比别人懂得多。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过也确实如此。

sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，从技术的角度来看，就像是把它塞进了一个应用里，你知道的，当你启动Facebook时，看起来你要去某个原生应用，

sentences.en: but it's really just taking you to a web page where, you know, the address bar and other things are hidden.
sentences.zh: 但实际上只是把你带到一个网页，在那里，你知道，地址栏和其他东西都被隐藏了。

sentences.en: So it just, it feels like, it feels like an app, but you're really, you're on the internet.
sentences.zh: 所以它就是，感觉像，感觉像一个应用，但实际上你，你在互联网上。

sentences.en: And the thing about it is on native, you know, and we could just argue this to death, like, like why, like whether this is a good idea or whether this can change,
sentences.zh: 关键在于，在原生端，你知道的，我们可以为这事争论不休，比如，为什么，比如这到底是不是个好主意，或者这能不能改变，

sentences.en: if it's, like, fundamental or not.
sentences.zh: 不管它是不是本质上的问题。

sentences.en: But the reality is the web experience on native sucks, right?
sentences.zh: 但现实是，原生端的网页体验糟透了，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, the Android browser, the Chrome on iOS and on Android and WebKit, all of it is kind of terrible.
sentences.zh: 比如，安卓浏览器、iOS和安卓上的Chrome以及WebKit，所有这些都有点糟糕。

sentences.en: And that's why Facebook bailed on the, you know, web, the web app app.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么Facebook放弃了，你知道的，网页，网页应用应用。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't say it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 我倒不会说它糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: It's terrible if you're trying to use, like, what we now accommodate as, like, an app.
sentences.zh: 如果你试图去用我们现在所理解的“应用”那种东西，那它确实糟糕。

sentences.en: Like, web app apps on those browsers are terrible.
sentences.zh: 比如，那些浏览器上的网页应用应用简直糟透了。

sentences.en: Let me think about that.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: Did I make that too many apps in a row?
sentences.zh: 我是不是连续用了太多次“应用”？

sentences.en: So, like, Gmail.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如，Gmail。

sentences.en: Like, Gmail.
sentences.zh: 比如，Gmail。

sentences.en: Like, I don't, my Gmail app, it is a website, but it's really an app.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不知道，我的Gmail应用，它是个网站，但它确实是个应用。

sentences.en: And to use that on those browsers is not a good experience for me.
sentences.zh: 在那些浏览器上使用它，对我的体验来说并不好。

sentences.en: But, like, going to a blog, for instance, like,
sentences.zh: 但是，比如，去看一个博客，举个例子，比如，

sentences.en: I think the normal ones are fine.
sentences.zh: 我觉得普通的博客挺正常的。

sentences.en: I actually don't like the apps that are, like, forum readers.
sentences.zh: 我其实不太喜欢那种论坛阅读器之类的应用。

sentences.en: They just don't work well for me.
sentences.zh: 它们对我来说就是不好用。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 对，这倒是个好点子。

sentences.en: So, maybe what it is, I think, actually, to be more specific,
sentences.zh: 所以，可能是这样的，我觉得，实际上，更具体地说，

sentences.en: I think that web app apps are in the uncanny valley where, like, you know, they respond pretty well and everything.
sentences.zh: 我觉得网页应用应用正处在恐怖谷里，你知道的，它们的响应速度挺快的，什么都挺好。

sentences.en: But when you, you know, say, flip a switch, and it's really just some kind of, like, JavaScript mock of what a native switch would look and feel like,
sentences.zh: 但当你，你知道的，比方说，拨动一个开关，而它实际上只是某种JavaScript模拟出来的、原生开关外观和感觉的东西时，

sentences.en: it behaves just slightly different.
sentences.zh: 它的表现就会有那么一点点不同。

sentences.en: And it's different enough that it makes you hate yourself.
sentences.zh: 而这种不同足以让你恨死自己。

sentences.en: It's in that uncanny valley.
sentences.zh: 它就处在那个恐怖谷里。

sentences.en: It's almost like if you get, like, a completely different experience on the web, you're much better off than trying to make it feel like a native app, you know?
sentences.zh: 这简直就像，如果你在网页上获得完全不同的体验，那可比费尽心思让它感觉像个原生应用要好得多，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Anyways, you don't have to do any of that nonsense because there's React native now.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，你没必要去搞那些无聊的东西，因为现在有了React Native。

sentences.en: It just came out.
sentences.zh: 它刚刚发布。

sentences.en: And so, the idea is similar to how React.js is this JavaScript library that lets you build a bunch of widgets programmatically.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个想法类似于React.js这个JavaScript库，它能让你以编程方式构建一堆小部件。

sentences.en: And, as the name suggests, all the widgets are reactive.
sentences.zh: 而且，顾名思义，所有的小部件都是响应式的。

sentences.en: So, if I wanted to make, say, a chat program, all I do is I say, hey, here's a chat widget.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我想做一个，比方说，聊天程序，我要做的就是说，嘿，这里有个聊天小部件。

sentences.en: It's backed by this array.
sentences.zh: 它由这个数组支撑。

sentences.en: Hey, here's a, you know, here's a button widget.
sentences.zh: 嘿，这里有个，你知道的，这里有个按钮小部件。

sentences.en: It's, you know, when you press it, this function gets called.
sentences.zh: 它，你知道的，当你按下它时，这个函数就会被调用。

sentences.en: And then, whenever, you know, you press the button, the function gets called.
sentences.zh: 然后，只要，你知道的，你按下了按钮，函数就会被调用。

sentences.en: That's pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 这挺清晰的。

sentences.en: But, also, whenever that array changes, it re-renders your chat window.
sentences.zh: 而且，每当那个数组发生变化时，它会重新渲染你的聊天窗口。

sentences.en: So, you don't have to say something like, you know, listen for new chat messages.
sentences.zh: 所以你不需要说诸如，你知道的，监听新的聊天消息之类的话。

sentences.en: When you get them, you know, clear out the window and redraw it.
sentences.zh: 当你收到它们时，你知道的，清空窗口并重新绘制。

sentences.en: Like, you just say, hey, look, this window is this chat array.
sentences.zh: 比如，你只要说，嘿，看，这个窗口就是这个聊天数组。

sentences.en: And it's just magically done.
sentences.zh: 然后它就神奇地完成了。

sentences.en: So, React Native is the same thing for Native.
sentences.zh: 所以，React Native对原生应用来说也是一样的道理。

sentences.en: And it's cross-platform.
sentences.zh: 而且它是跨平台的。

sentences.en: So, what these guys have done is they've defined, like, you know, like a button in this React JavaScript language.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些家伙做的事是，他们定义了，就像，你知道的，在这个React JavaScript语言中定义一个按钮。

sentences.en: And they've kept it very similar to the web.
sentences.zh: 并且他们让它与网页保持高度相似。

sentences.en: There are some differences of things which just didn't translate well.
sentences.zh: 有些地方有些差异，因为有些东西转换过来效果不好。

sentences.en: But some things like buttons are almost exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 但像按钮这样的一些东西几乎完全一样。

sentences.en: So, you define some button in React.js.
sentences.zh: 所以，你在React.js中定义一个按钮。

sentences.en: And then, on Android, you get a native Android button.
sentences.zh: 然后，在安卓上，你会得到一个原生的安卓按钮。

sentences.en: And then, on iOS, you get, you know, the iOS button.
sentences.zh: 然后，在iOS上，你会得到，你知道的，iOS按钮。

sentences.en: And if you define a widget like Map, for example, you'll get the, you know, native Apple Maps on iOS.
sentences.zh: 如果你定义了一个像地图这样的小部件，例如，你会得到，你知道的，iOS上的原生Apple地图。

sentences.en: And you'll get the native Google Maps on Android.
sentences.zh: 而在安卓上你会得到原生的Google地图。

sentences.en: So, they, you know, try their best to, like, you know, do the right thing there.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们，你知道的，尽最大努力，去，你知道的，在那儿做出正确的处理。

sentences.en: And it's all reactive, like I said.
sentences.zh: 而且就像我说的，这一切都是响应式的。

sentences.en: So, you know, you could have a map widget.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你可以有一个地图小部件。

sentences.en: And you can say, okay, I have this location variable.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，好的，我有一个位置变量。

sentences.en: And whenever this location variable changes, recenter my map.
sentences.zh: 每当这个位置变量改变时，就重新居中我的地图。

sentences.en: And it just magically works.
sentences.zh: 然后它就神奇地起作用了。

sentences.en: So, it's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 所以，这挺酷的。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's actually, I don't think it's out yet.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是不是真的，我觉得它好像还没发布。

sentences.en: So, just read some articles on it.
sentences.zh: 所以，只是读了一些关于它的文章。

sentences.en: You know, they have Facebook put out some videos.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，Facebook发布了一些视频。

sentences.en: And be ready.
sentences.zh: 准备好迎接吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: So, our next article is Windows 10.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的下一篇文章是关于Windows 10的。

sentences.en: And the exciting thing everyone wants to talk about about Windows 10 is the fact that Microsoft is moving to a free for consumers asterisk.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想谈论的关于Windows 10的最让人兴奋的事情是，微软正对消费者实行免费政策（带星号）。

sentences.en: All sorts of caveats, potentially, whether that's true or not.
sentences.zh: 潜在地包含各种附加条件，不管这是否属实。

sentences.en: But the long story short is that it appears that Windows instead of, or Microsoft, sorry,
sentences.zh: 但长话短说，情况似乎是Windows而不是，或者微软，抱歉，

sentences.en: instead of trying to gain a lot of money from selling new versions of Windows and waiting for people to upgrade,
sentences.zh: 与其试图通过销售新版本的Windows赚大钱并等待人们升级，

sentences.en: to try to make sure everyone's upgraded on to something vaguely resembling the latest version, as opposed to tons of people still running Windows XP,
sentences.zh: 与其试图确保每个人都升级到某种勉强类似于最新版本的系统，而不是成千上万的人仍然在运行Windows XP，

sentences.en: is to offer Windows 10 free as an upgrade to people who have, I think, at least Windows 7, if I read correctly.
sentences.zh: 不如把Windows 10作为免费升级提供给那些拥有，我想，至少是Windows 7（如果我没记错的话）的人。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, if you have Windows 7 or later license, you can upgrade to Windows 10 for free.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你拥有Windows 7或更高版本的许可证，你可以免费升级到Windows 10。

sentences.en: And then it looks like they're moving towards updating again for free.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来他们正朝着继续免费更新的方向发展。

sentences.en: So, instead of having very long-lasting OSs, it sounds like their intention is to move to kind of a more frequent cycle.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其拥有生命周期很长的操作系统，听起来他们的意图是转向一种更频繁的周期。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then that way that they can, again, push features and keep people on something, akin to what you get on Android or iOS, right?
sentences.zh: 这样一来，他们又可以推送功能，让人们保持使用某种系统，类似于你在安卓或iOS上获得的体验，对吧？

sentences.en: Instead of your computer just coming with an OS and just sticking with it.
sentences.zh: 而不是你的电脑自带一个操作系统就一直用到底。

sentences.en: If you, OSX does something similar, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你看，OS X也做了类似的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Like they update, what is it, about once a year or once every other year?
sentences.zh: 比如他们更新，是多少，大约一年一次或每两年一次？

sentences.en: It depends.
sentences.zh: 这得看情况。

sentences.en: Much more frequent than Windows from Microsoft.
sentences.zh: 比微软的Windows频繁得多。

sentences.en: And so, everyone's kind of assumed to be running something that is pretty new.
sentences.zh: 所以，大家都默认在使用相当新的系统。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 对，这挺酷的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a chicken and egg problem that this solves, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这解决了一个先有鸡还是先有蛋的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is developers are sitting on Windows XP or Windows 7.
sentences.zh: 那就是开发者们还停留在Windows XP或Windows 7上。

sentences.en: They're making apps using that.
sentences.zh: 他们正在用那些系统制作应用。

sentences.en: So, of course, they're really interested in backwards compatibility.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，他们对向下兼容非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And then, you know, you end up with no one having any reason to update.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，结果就是没有人有任何理由去更新。

sentences.en: Like, you know, as soon as a program, like if tomorrow Steam told me, hey, you know, to run Steam, you need to have Windows 10.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，一旦有个程序，比如如果明天Steam告诉我，嘿，你知道的，要运行Steam，你需要有Windows 10。

sentences.en: Well, then, shoot, I'm going on Windows 10.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那糟了，我得换Windows 10。

sentences.en: I mean, I have no choice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我别无选择。

sentences.en: And so, that's sort of, I think, the environment that they want to cultivate.
sentences.zh: 所以，这某种程度上，我认为，就是他们想要培育的环境。

sentences.en: One where, you know, there's no reason for people who already have Windows to not be on the lateSt.
sentences.zh: 一个让那些已经拥有Windows的人没有理由不使用最新版本的环境。

sentences.en: And then, once, you know, say 90% of people running Windows are running 10, then developers can start saying, well,
sentences.zh: 然后，一旦，你知道的，比方说90%运行Windows的人都在用10，那么开发者就可以开始说，好吧，

sentences.en: why am I going to support 7 if you could just go to 10 for free and everyone's done it?
sentences.zh: 既然大家都能免费升级到10而且都升级了，我为什么还要支持7呢？

sentences.en: So, then, you know, you'll see developers dropping support for older versions of Windows.
sentences.zh: 所以，然后，你知道的，你会看到开发者放弃对旧版本Windows的支持。

sentences.en: And that will, you know, force more people to upgrade and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 而这又会，你知道的，迫使更多人升级，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, and I think it's, you know, the other strategic thing for Microsoft is they want to start getting into this cloud business.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，对微软来说另一个战略举措是他们想进军云端业务。

sentences.en: Like, they want to compete with Dropbox on, you know, cloud sharing and things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们想在云共享等方面与Dropbox竞争。

sentences.en: And so, you know, let's say something else comes out that's like Dropbox, but different.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，假设出现了另一个像Dropbox但又不同的东西。

sentences.en: Like, it's, you know, it's a service.
sentences.zh: 比如，它，你知道的，它是一个服务。

sentences.en: You know, it's like some kind of desktop app you download.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像你下载的某种桌面应用。

sentences.en: But instead of synchronizing your files, it synchronizes your contacts.
sentences.zh: 但它不同步你的文件，而是同步你的联系人。

sentences.en: Okay, so it's contact box.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也就是联系人盒子。

sentences.en: Then, like, you know, if Windows, if Microsoft sees, oh, that's a pretty cool desktop app, they could bake it into Windows 11.
sentences.zh: 然后，就像，你知道的，如果Windows，如果微软看到，哦，那是个挺酷的桌面应用，他们可以把它内置到Windows 11里。

sentences.en: They could come up with Microsoft contact box and it's part of the OS and they can kind of run these people out, which is something they haven't been able to do in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 他们可以推出微软联系人盒子，作为操作系统的一部分，然后他们就可以把这些人挤出市场，这是他们在过去一直做不到的事。

sentences.en: So, strategically, it's a really good decision.
sentences.zh: 所以，从战略上讲，这是一个非常明智的决定。

sentences.en: It probably should have been made like 20 years ago, but I guess we'll let it slide.
sentences.zh: 这大概在20年就该做了，不过我想我们就不深究了。

sentences.en: So, then, the next article, this is pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 那么，接下来的一篇文章，这个挺酷的。

sentences.en: I never knew this existed, but...
sentences.zh: 我以前从不知道这东西存在，但是……

sentences.en: So, if you're writing JavaScript right now on the web, you're writing ECMAScript 5.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你现在在网页上写JavaScript，你写的是ECMAScript 5。

sentences.en: And so, the deal is, you know, ECMAScript is like the formal definition of JavaScript, like the formal name of that language.
sentences.zh: 所以情况是这样的，你知道，ECMAScript就像是JavaScript的正式定义，就像是该语言的正式名称。

sentences.en: And most people are writing 5.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都在写5。

sentences.en: Now, they're coming out with, you know, the JavaScript version 6.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们推出了，你知道的，JavaScript第6版。

sentences.en: Actually, it's already out.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它已经发布了。

sentences.en: But the problem is, you know, again, you have this adoption problem.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，你知道的，又来了，你面临着普及率的问题。

sentences.en: Like, if I write it in 6, you know, 90% of the people aren't going to be able to use my website.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我用6来写，你知道的，90%的人将无法使用我的网站。

sentences.en: And so, that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是个问题。

sentences.en: So, they wrote this transpiler.
sentences.zh: 于是他们写了这个转译器。

sentences.en: So, basically, you can write your code as if everyone's running the latest bleeding edge, you know, Chrome or Firefox.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，你可以编写你的代码，就好像每个人都在运行最新、最尖端的，你知道的，Chrome或Firefox一样。

sentences.en: And for people who aren't, they can run the JavaScript 5 version of your code.
sentences.zh: 而对于那些没有的人，他们可以运行你的代码的JavaScript 5版本。

sentences.en: And maybe it's a little slower or something like that, but functionally, it should do exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 也许它会稍微慢一点或者诸如此类，但在功能上，它应该做完全相同的事情。

sentences.en: And it allows you to sort of make that transition and start writing JavaScript 6 now.
sentences.zh: 它允许你进行那种过渡，并从现在开始编写JavaScript 6。

sentences.en: It's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 这挺酷的。

sentences.en: Very nice.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.zh: 到了本期图书推荐时间。

sentences.zh: 本，本，本，本，本期图书推荐。

sentences.zh: 本期图书推荐。

sentences.zh: 我推荐的这本书，跟平时有点不太一样。

sentences.en: But I actually found out that there's this magazine called Game Developer Magazine.
sentences.zh: 但我其实发现了一本叫做《游戏开发者杂志》的杂志。

sentences.en: And they stopped printing issues, I think, like, five, six years ago.
sentences.zh: 他们好像在五、六年前就停止印刷实体版了。

sentences.en: But you can actually get all of the issues for free.
sentences.zh: 但你实际上可以免费获得所有的期数。

sentences.en: So, it's pretty cool.
sentences.zh: 所以，这挺酷的。

sentences.en: I mean, you can just flip through literally any issue of this magazine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以翻阅这本杂志的字面意义上的任何一期。

sentences.en: You can just download it and flip through a PDF of it.
sentences.zh: 你只需下载它并翻阅它的PDF版本。

sentences.en: So, if you're into game development or you're into sort of the history of game development, things like that, this is a pretty cool resource to check out.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你喜欢游戏开发，或者你喜欢游戏开发的历史之类的东西，这是一个非常酷的资源，值得一看。
